Judgment

This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 01-05-2024 at about 10.45 a.m., the petitioner was riding the TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA-17-HG-0707, slowly, cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, near Kere Koodi Basavanna Temple, Jagalur-Kottur road, Jagalur Town,
Davanagere.

At that time, all of a sudden a water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353,
which was driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and dashed against the TVS XL Moped of the petitioner.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Jagalur, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Puttur Hospital, Hosapete, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
Earlier to the accident, he was working as mason and was earning Rs.1,200/- per day.
But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity.
The Jagalur Police have registered the case against the driver of the said water tanker for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest.
3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.
4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

He has contended that, the petitioner was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner,

sentences.text: But, the petitioner colluding with the jurisdictional police has lodged a false case and filed a false charge-sheet against the driver of water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353, with an intention to have illegal gain.

Further it is contended that, in the alleged accident the petitioner has not sustained injury and the petitioner colluding with the hospital authorities has got created additional medical bills with a sole intention to get more compensation from this respondent.

Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident he had valid vehicle documents and his vehicle was insured by the respondent No.2 insurance company and the same was valid from 04-03- 2024 to 03-03-2025.
The permit, driving licence and other documents were also in force.
If this Hon'ble Court come to a conclusion that the petitioner is entitled for compensation, the respondent No.2 insurance is solely responsible to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the present claim petition is liable to be dismissed against respondent No.1.
For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. Whereas, respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.

It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.3008/241308407/02/000 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 and its validity,
subject to terms and conditions, exceptions, limits and endorsement of the policy and subject to compliance of 64-VB of Insurance Act.
Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act.

Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HG-707 which involved in the alleged accident, they are also proper and necessary parties to the present proceedings to adjudicate the controversy involved in the case.
It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident and involvement of vehicle bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 as alleged in the claim petition.
Further it is contended that, after lapse of 2 days the petitioner has filed a false case against the said vehicle to cause wrongful loss to this respondent.

Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1 has willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and allowed him to ply the said vehicle on the road without having valid and effective permit, fitness certificate and converting the vehicle illegally as water tanker, as against its authorization.
The respondent No.1 has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Section 150(2) of Amended Motor Vehicles Act, 2019.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation in view of amended provision of Motor Vehicle Act, with effect from 01-04-2022, in the above matter.
Further it is contended that, the alleged accident has not occurred in the manner as pleaded by the petitioner.
The alleged accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner and he has attributed more contributory negligence in the cause of accident.
Further, he was riding the motorcycle without holding driving licence, insurance policy and without wearing safety head gear.
Thus, he being guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and regulations, is not entitled to seek for compensation from this respondent.
There was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the water tanker.
It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

12. On meticulously going through the above police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7 and 12 to 14,
prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 and dashing the same to motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-17-HG-0707 of the petitioner from the opposite direction.
Due to said impact the petitioner has fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

The investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.14, has clearly stated that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353.

At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.1 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

But, the respondent No.1 & 2 have specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the alleged accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-17- HG-0707 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353.
But, the respondents have failed to establish the said contentions.
They have neither adduced any evidence, nor they have produced any document to establish the said contentions
Even, the respondents have not stepped into witness box to depose the above contentions on oath.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 and dashing the same to the motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HG- 0707 of the petitioner from opposite direction.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of the petitioner/rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-17- HG-0707 himself or there was any contributory negligence on his part in the cause of accident.

14. Further, the Ex.P.3 sketch and Ex.P.4 spot mahazar also clearly speaks that, the said accident has taken place on the left side of 16 feet wide Jagalur-Kottur road, near Kere Kodi Basavanna Temple,
Jagalur Town, Davanagere District, in between offending water tanker bearing No.KA- 17-TD-2353 and oncoming motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA- 17-HG-0707 of the petitioner.
As per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353.

Further, the investigation officer in his final report, marked as Ex.P.14, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and Somla Naik vs Manjunath S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7377407/

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. No doubt, there is a delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
But, the complainant has stated the reason for delay in lodging the complaint in his Ex.P.2 first information statement.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing treatment to the petitioner in the hospital, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
It is settled proposition of law that, the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases.

entities.text: Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident.
The treatment of victim is given priority over lodging FIR.
The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR.
Hence, delay in lodging FIR not a ground to dismiss claim petition."

16. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record by the respondents to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.1 First Information Report and Ex.P.2 first information statement.

In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.

17. Further, on meticulously going through the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries, Ex.P.10 referral card, Ex.P.11 OPD slip, Ex.P.18 x-rays, Ex.P.19 OPD book and Ex.P.20 x-ray, it clearly reveals that, the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner has sustained compound segmental fracture shaft of right tibia.

The P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner has sustained above injuries in the road traffic accident.
Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross-examined P.W.2 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth, which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the petitioner.

Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.

18. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,

Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.
21. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue this Court has come to conclusion that, the accident in question has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 and the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident.
The medical records placed on record clearly speaks that, the petitioner has sustained compound segmental fracture shaft of right tibia and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.

Therefore,
this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.

The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
22. Towards loss of future income:
In order to determine the compensation towards loss of future income, the age, monthly income and disability of the petitioner are to be determined.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the notarised copy of his Aadhar card, which is marked as Ex.P.15.
As per Ex.P.15, the date of birth of the petitioner is 01-01-1969.
The accident has taken place on 01-05-2024 at about 10:45 a.m.
This clearly goes to show that, the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident was 55 years.

Further, the P.W.2, who is the doctor who has examined the petitioner for the purpose of assessment of disability, has clearly deposed in his examination-in-chief affidavit that, on clinical examination he found that, the petitioner has suffered compound segmental fracture shaft of right tibia.

Further he has deposed that, on clinical and radiological examination of injuries sustained by the petitioner he found that, there is 41% physical disability to right lower limb and 21% physical disability to the whole body of the petitioner.

Further, the Ex.P.7 wound certificate, Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries (total 2), Ex.P.10 referral card, Ex.P.11 OPD slip,
Ex.P.18 x-rays (total 7), Ex.P.19 OPD book and Ex.P.20 x-ray clearly speaks that, the petitioner has suffered the above stated injuries and for the said injuries he has undergone surgery.
The P.W.2 has clearly denied the suggestions made to him that, the petitioner has not suffered any disability and he has exaggerated the percentage of disability.

Further he has stated that, the petitioner requires to Somla Naik vs Manjunath S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7377407/
7 undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
This clearly goes to show that, the disability has been assessed before the completion of full treatment to the petitioner.
As per the gazette notification issued by the Ministry of Social Justice of Government of India, the disability should be assessed after completion of treatment.

If the disability had been assessed after future surgery,
perhaps there would have been reduction in the percentage of the disability.

Further, it is pertinent to note that, the P.W.2 has deposed in his evidence that, the accident has occurred on 01-05- 2024 and he has assessed the disability to the petitioner on 06-06-2025, which is after lapse of one year and one month from the date of injuries caused to the petitioner.

Further, it is pertinent to note that,
P.W.2 has clearly stated in his cross-examination that, the petitioner has sustained one fracture at the middle of the tibia and another at ankle joint and out of those fractures one is united and two fractures are mal-united.

Further, he has clearly admitted that, there is no shortening of limb, there is no loss of bone, the mal- union of the fractures can be corrected by undergoing further surgery,
the range of movement of hip is normal, there is loss of range of movement to the extent of 8% at knee and 9% at the ankle joint and there are no complications at the fracture part except mal-union..
Further he has admitted that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability,

Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
23. The petitioner has deposed in his evidence that, before accident he was working as mason and was earning Rs.1,200/- per day.
Further he has deposed that, due to grievous injuries suffered in the said accident he is unable to do his work.
The respondent No.2 has specifically denied the same.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as mason and was earning Rs.1,200/- per day.

Therefore, in such circumstances, there is no other option before this Court,
except to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
The accident took place in 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner at Rs.1,98,000/-.

24. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 55 years is 11.

Therefore, taking into consideration the injuries sustained and disability suffered by the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, an compensation amount of Rs.60,000/- is to be awarded to the petitioner towards pain and sufferings.
27. Attendant charges:
As per Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 10 days in Puttur Hospital, Hosapete.
He might have spent considerable amount towards attendant charges during that period.

Therefore, compensation of Rs.1000 x 10 =
Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards the attendant charges.
28. Food and nourishment:
As per Ex.P.8 and 9 discharge summaries, the petitioner has taken treatment as in-patient for 10 days in Puttur Hospital, Hosapete.
He might have spent considerable amount towards food and nourishment during that period.
Therefore, compensation of Rs.800 x 10 = Rs.8,000/- is awarded towards food and nourishment charges.
29. Conveyance expenses:

The petitioner is the resident of Venkateshapura Tanda, Gurusiddapura Post, Jagalur Taluk, Davanagere, the accident has taken place on Jagalur- Kottur road, near Kere Kodi Basavanna Temple, Jagalur Town, Davanagere District and the petitioner has taken treatment at Puttur Hospital, Hosapete.

Taking into consideration the distance in between the above places,
compensation of Rs.10,000/- is awarded towards conveyance.
30. Loss of income during treatment period:
The petitioner has taken treatment for 10 days as in-patient at Puttur Hospital, Hosapete, for the grievous injury sustained by him.
He might have taken rest for about 2 months and lost his income for the said period.

Therefore, Rs.16,500 x 2 =
Rs.33,000/- is awarded towards loss of income during treatment period.
31. Loss of amenities:

It is evident from the documents placed on record that, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 55 years and unfortunately he has suffered compound segmental fracture shaft of right tibia.
Further, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.
Therefore, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- towards loss of amenities would be just and reasonable.
32. Future medical expenses:
The P.W.2 has clearly deposed in his evidence that, the petitioner needs to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants, which would cost around Rs.40,000/-.
But, admittedly the P.W.2 has not issued estimation of cost for the said surgery.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medical expenses would be just and reasonable.

34. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-17-TD- 2353.

The insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 vide policy bearing No.3008/241308407/02/000,
in respect of offending water tanker, was valid from 04-03-2024 to 03- 03-2025.
As such, the insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 in respect of offending vehicle was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 01-05-2024.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.

Further,
the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-17-TD-2353 the accident in question has taken place.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.6,84,041/-,
with interest at the rate of 6% per annum (excluding interest on future medical expenses of Rs.20,000/-), from the date of petition till its realization, from the respondent No.2, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
35. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.
But, the petitioner colluding with the jurisdictional police has lodged a false case and filed a false charge-sheet against the driver of water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353, with an intention to have illegal gain.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The respondent No.1 has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Section 150(2) of Amended Motor Vehicles Act, 2019.
Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation in view of amended provision of Motor Vehicle Act, with effect from 01-04-2022, in the above matter.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 01-05-2024 at about 10.45 a.m., near Kere Kodi Basavanna Temple, Jagalur- Kottur road, Jagalur Town, Davanagere, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Water Tanker bearing registration No.KA-17-TD-2353 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
As per the Motor Vehicle Accident Report, which is marked as Ex.P.6, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.
When the accident was not caused due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the rider of the motorcycle, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353.
Admittedly,
the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and injuries caused to the petitioner in the said accident.
15. No doubt, there is a delay of 2 days in lodging the complaint by the petitioner.
He has clearly stated that, as he was engaged in providing treatment to the petitioner in the hospital, there is delay caused in lodging the complaint.
16. There is absolutely no rebuttal evidence on record by the respondents to disbelieve the reason for delay in lodging the complaint, stated in the Ex.P.1 First Information Report and Ex.P.2 first information statement.
In such circumstances and in the light of ratio laid down in the above cited decision, this Court is of the opinion that, in the present facts and circumstances of the case, the delay for lodging the complaint is properly explained by the petitioner with cogent and satisfactory reasons.
The petitioner has sustained compound segmental fracture shaft of right tibia.
On the other hand, there is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the petitioner.
Therefore, in such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioner regarding rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the said accident.
18. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
Somla Naik vs Manjunath S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7377407/
6 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required."
Therefore,
this Court is of the further opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under various heads.
The damages are to be assessed under two heads i.e. pecuniary damages, such as medical treatment, attendants, transport, actual loss of earning, future loss of earning etc., and non-pecuniary damages, such as mental and physical shock, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life, loss of prospects of marriage etc.
Further he has admitted that, he has assessed only physical disability and not functional disability,
Therefore, in such circumstances and taking into consideration the age of the petitioner, injuries sustained, avocation of the petitioner, duration of treatment and oral and documentary evidence available on record, this Court is of the opinion that, considering the physical disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner would be justified.
Hence, in the instant case the disability of 15% to the whole body of the petitioner is considered.
In such circumstances, the burden was on the petitioner to prove his avocation and income.
But, the petitioner has failed to establish the same through cogent and corroborative evidence.
He has not produced any document to show that, before accident he was working as mason and was earning Rs.1,200/- per day.
The accident took place in 2024.
Hence, the notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,500/- per month and the annual income of the petitioner at Rs.1,98,000/-.
Further, there is no evidence on record to show that, there is breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy by the insured/respondent No.1.
Further,
the evidence placed on record by the petitioner clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-17-TD-2353 the accident in question has taken place.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
